```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's core product, threshold and nexus monitoring, is given away free by Kintsugi, Numeral and TaxJar as a funnel into their paid filing services. A paid standalone monitor is competing against $0 offers from better-resourced firms with fresher threshold data.",
    "Idea A also faces a structural substitute. The brief cites indie founders solving the problem by moving to a Merchant of Record (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy), which removes the need for a monitor at all.",
    "Idea A's segment is described as having low willingness to pay until revenue grows. At that point founders either qualify for competitors' free tiers or need filing, which the monitor does not provide. The payer squeeze runs in both directions.",
    "Idea B's payer is an engineering or platform lead with a CI tooling budget. Pricing is anchored at $20-50 per developer per month (Harness add-ons), and Testhide shows a paid self-serve tier exists at $49/mo cloud. That is a higher revenue ceiling per customer than A.",
    "Idea B's demand evidence is broader and quantitative: an analysis of 20.2M CI jobs naming flaky tests as a top cause of blocked PRs, plus practitioner quotes. Idea A's evidence is two qualitative blog or forum quotes, one from 2020.",
    "Idea B's free competitors are mostly unmonetized OSS clones and enterprise contact-sales incumbents. That leaves a plausible self-serve paid wedge for small and mid-size teams. Idea A's free competitors already target its exact segment.",
    "Idea B's trust and false-negative risk can be partly avoided by shipping flaky-test flagging as an advisory signal before any gating, which the brief raises as an open question. Idea A has no comparable workaround for its pricing problem."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's main feasibility and willingness-to-pay signal is Tax Threshold Radar at $49/mo. The brief says its testimonials could not be verified and it may be an unvalidated landing page (Open question 3). It cannot be counted as proof that anyone pays for monitoring-only.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Idea B carries serious risks that threaten the 90-day target: a crowded field of near-identical OSS tools, a cold-start problem with no historical data, a buyer requirement for trust that may take months to earn, and security and DPA reviews before pipeline access. B's six-week MVP claim is unsourced and counts as missing. B wins mainly because A's case against is more decisive (free incumbents plus Merchant of Record substitution), not because B is clearly validated."
}
```
